subject: Renewal proposal: partial-commit to usage blend + fixed bridge
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: partial-commit to usage blend + fixed bridge

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the time on Friday. Per our discussion, I put together a proposal that blends a smaller committed seat of Dedicated capacity for the next 24 months with a usage layer for spiky workloads and a 6‑month fixed bridge credit to smooth cashflow into your fiscal year. High level: 

- Year 1: 40% committed (reserved GPU pool), 60% usage (on-demand API) with blended unit price; 6‑month bridge credit representing ~10% of ARR to offset transition costs.
- Year 2: Option to re-balance to 60% committed / 40% usage or convert to straight usage-only depending on observed token run-rate.
- Auto-renew: standard opt-in. We can add an auto‑opt-out trigger if usage drops below 30% of baseline for two consecutive months.

Attached: RDW_AtlasData_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf and a usage-blend-pricing-model.xlsx with worked examples using your June workload.

Two asks: (1) Confirm whether accounting prefers a single annual invoice or quarterly invoices for the committed portion; (2) If you want the 6‑month bridge as a credit on invoice or an upfront discount.

Happy to hop on a quick call this week to walk through the model line by line.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | High-performance inference for production
From: Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasdata.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@atlasdata.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: partial-commit to usage blend + fixed bridge

Diego —

Thanks for this. The blended approach looks promising given our bursty ETL jobs. A few clarifying questions from finance and infra: 

1) Can you show the P&L impact if we frontload 75% of the committed vCPUs in Q1 (we prefer predictable capacity during our ingestion window)?
2) For the 6‑month bridge credit, we need it to appear as a separate credit line on the invoice (not a discount applied to unit price).
3) Auto-renew: we need an explicit 60‑day notification before renewal and the opt-out trigger to be timezone-agnostic for our EU pipelines.

We also want to involve security for the private deployment checklist if we convert more committed capacity in year 2. Can you loop in someone from your security team?

—Sarah
Sarah Liu, Head of Data Platforms, Atlas Data
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal: partial-commit to usage blend + fixed bridge

Team — forwarding Sarah's questions. Key asks: show P&L for Q1 frontload of 75% committed, bridge credit shown as separate credit line, and 60‑day explicit renewal notice + EU timezone opt-out trigger. Also they want security on the thread for a potential private deployment in year 2.

My suggested path:
- Use a 24‑month term but allow a rebalancing window at 12 months. That gives us leverage to lock in slightly better committed pricing while preserving a usage escape hatch.
- For accounting, default to quarterly invoice for committed portion but offer annual invoice if they accept upfront payment.
- Bridge credit as invoice line is straightforward; finance can handle.

Karthik / Marissa: can you run two quick scenarios in the pricing model (attached) — (A) 75% frontloaded in Q1 with quarterly invoicing; (B) 40/60 for year 1 with the bridge as a credit line. Ask Rishi to review the legal redline on the renewal notice language.

Thanks —
Diego
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@atlasdata.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 15:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: partial-commit to usage blend + fixed bridge

Sarah / all —

I ran the two scenarios in the attached spreadsheet and summarized below (numbers are illustrative and in USD):

Scenario A — Q1 frontload (75% committed)
- Year 1 committed ARR: $480k (75% of baseline). Usage spend for spikes: ~$160k. Bridge credit: $60k applied as an invoice credit across first two quarters.
- Net cashflow: earlier recognition in Q1 (positive for Atlas's capacity planning).
- Effective unit price: ~12% lower on committed tokens vs blended scenario.

Scenario B — 40/60 year 1 with bridge credit as separate invoice line
- Year 1 committed ARR: $256k. Usage spend estimated $384k. Bridge credit: $60k as separate credit line on Q1 invoice.
- Net cashflow: more even across the year, lower upfront but higher variable spend risk.

Operational notes:
- We can guarantee capacity for the Q1 frontload with a dedicated pool and an SLA for ingestion windows; will need to document preferred regions and queueing behavior.
- Renewal notice language (proposed): "Redwood will send written notice of intent to renew no less than 60 days prior to the term expiration. Customer may elect to opt-out within 30 days of notice." Rishi — can you tweak to make timezone-agnostic language?

Sarah — attaching the updated usage-blend-pricing-model.xlsx with both scenarios. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30‑minute walk-through where I share the spreadsheet and the invoice mock-ups.

Best,
Karthik
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasdata.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: partial-commit to usage blend + fixed bridge

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear asks. A couple legal points and our proposed clean language to include in the SOW/amendment: 

1) Renewal notice: "Redwood will provide written notice of renewal at least sixty (60) calendar days prior to the end of the then-current term. The Customer shall have thirty (30) calendar days from the date of such notice to notify Redwood of its intent not to renew; otherwise, the term shall automatically renew on the same basis (subject to any previously agreed pricing adjustments)."

2) Bridge credit: Redwood will record the bridge as a distinct credit line on the invoice for the first two quarters of Year 1. The credit is non‑refundable and will be applied to Atlas Data's invoice balance.

3) Frontload capacity: if Atlas elects the 75% Q1 frontload, Redwood will reserve the committed pool and enact a quarterly invoicing cadence unless Atlas elects an upfront annual invoice in writing.

4) Security: copying our security contact separately (cc'd offline) to start a Private Deployment checklist for year‑2 conversion — items to cover: VPC peering options, KMS integration, audit log retention, SOC2 evidence.

If that language looks good to you, we'll prepare an amendment and a clean SOW and send it for signature.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
